Scheme Name: Establishment Of Small Scale Dairy Unit (SSDU) Short Title: SSDU Detailed Description: The "Small Scale Dairy Unit (SSDU)" has been launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, U.T. Administration of Daman & Diu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli. It aims to promote dairy development by supporting the establishment of a small-scale dairy unit with indigenous Gir cows. Through this scheme, financial assistance in the form of capital subsidy and back-ended subsidy is provided to beneficiaries for the purchase of milch cows, construction of cattle sheds, and procurement of feed, equipment, and insurance coverage. Eligibility Criteria: 1. The applicant must be a resident of the Union Territory of Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. 1. The applicant should establish a small-scale dairy unit with 10 milch cows. 1. The applicant should procure indigenous Gir breed cows only. 1. The applicant should avail a bank loan for implementation of the project. 1. The applicant should utilise the subsidy strictly for approved components. 1. The applicant should maintain records as per the General Financial Rules, 1963. > **Preference / Reservation / Relaxation:** The applicant belonging to the Scheduled Caste or the Scheduled Tribe category is eligible for a higher subsidy rate under the back-ended subsidy and insurance components.

Scheme Name: Scheme for Loan and Subsidy for Manure and Fertilizer-DNH&DD Short Title: SLSMF Detailed Description: The scheme “Scheme for Loan and Subsidy for Manure and Fertilizer” has been implemented by the Agriculture Department, UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. It aims to encourage the use of fertilizers so as to improve productivity. Through this scheme, manure and fertilizers are provided to Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and non-SC/ST small and marginal farmers having land holdings up to 2 hectares on subsidy-cum-loan basis. The scheme is implemented by the Agriculture Department through field-level functionaries. Manures and fertilisers are provided to eligible cultivators on a 40% subsidy and 60% loan basis. The assistance is given in kind and not in cash. The quantity of fertilizers is limited as per the prescribed crop-wise rates. The scheme focuses on supporting small and marginal farmers to enhance agricultural output. Eligibility Criteria: 1. The applicant should be a cultivator or farmer. 1. The applicant should belong to categories such as Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), or original farmers (as mentioned). 1. The applicant should have a land holding of up to 2 hectares. 1. The applicant should be engaged in agricultural activities requiring fertilisers or manure.
Benefits: Provision of Manure and Fertilizers Manures and fertilizers will be provided to eligible cultivators. Assistance is given in kind and not in cash. Subsidy and Loan Component Assistance is provided on a 40% subsidy and 60% loan basis. Crop-wise Fertilizer Quantity (in Nutrients) Paddy: Nitrogen 110, Phosphorus 60, Potash 60 Maize: Nitrogen 100, Phosphorus 50 Groundnut: Nitrogen 25, Phosphorus 50 Castor: Nitrogen 20, Phosphorus 20 Wheat: Nitrogen 100, Phosphorus 50, Potash 50 Sugarcane: Nitrogen 250, Phosphorus 125, Potash 125 Green Manuring Support 40 kg of seeds per hectare will be supplied for green manuring. Loan Recovery Provision The loan amount shall be recovered in one instalment after completion of the season. Season-wise Recovery Period Kharif (June to July): Recovery from December to February Rabi (October to November): Recovery from March to May Hot Weather (January to February): Recovery from June to July Interest and Penalty Condition Interest rate will be as prescribed by the Government of India from time to time. In case of default, penal interest at 2½% will be charged. Recovery will be made as arrears of land revenue.

Scheme Name: Financial Assistance to Boat owner / Fishermen Captured by Pakistan Marine Security Agency (PMSA)-DNH&DD Short Title: FABOFPAK Detailed Description: The scheme “Financial Assistance to Boat owner / Fishermen Captured by Pakistan Marine Security Agency (PMSA)” has been implemented by the Department of Fisheries, UT Administration of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. The scheme aims to help the families of the fishermen affected due to captured by Pakistani Marine Security Agency. Ameliorate the hardship due to apprehension/detention of the fishing vessel, by providing one time back ended financial assistance to the registered and licensed fishing vessel owners operating from the Union Territory to re-construct/replace their fishing boat/engine etc. Eligibility Criteria: 1. The applicant must be a resident of the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. 1. The applicant must be a boat owner or fisherman captured by the Pakistan Marine Security Agency (PMSA), or a family member thereof.
Benefits: Pattern of Assistance: Unskilled daily wages rate as notified time to time by the U. T. Administration to the families of the Fishermen those are held 1s time captive/detained by Pakistani Marine Security Agency (PMSA), having valid ID Cards and resident of U.T. of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. T.A./D.A. to the fishermen during the repatriations from Pakistani Jail:- Travelling Allowance (T.A.) is admissible at 2nd class Sleeper of Railways Fair. Daily Allowance (D.A.) of ₹250/- per day per person is admissible during repatriation. One time financial Assistance in the form of back ended subsidy to the registered boat owner of the U.T. of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu to re-construct/ replace their fishing vessels by new fishing vessels @ 25% maximum up to ₹ 10.00 lakh, with waiting period of five years.

Scheme Name: Establishment of Small Scale Poultry Unit (Layer) for livestock owner of Daman & Diu Short Title: ESSPULODD Detailed Description: The scheme "Establishment of Small Scale Poultry Unit (Layer) for livestock owners of Daman & Diu" has been launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, U.T. Administration of Daman & Diu. It aims Economic up-liftmen of the SC/ST, SMF, and BPL Families. Financial assistance in the form of 50% subsidy is provided for the construction of a poultry shed, purchase of pullets (18–21 weeks), poultry equipments and feed for 4 months. The scheme beneficiaries can avail the benefit for two years or till becoming self-sufficient. Units must be operated on scientific lines, and beneficiaries must supply surplus eggs to nearby schools under the Mid-Day Meals Scheme, with fortnightly payment made by the Extension Officer (Dairy) or Veterinary Officer (DP). Objectives Economic upliftment of the SC/ST, SMF, and BPL Families. To provide protein-rich food to the SC/ST, SMF, and BPL through eggs. To provide a regular supply of healthy eggs under the Scheme of Mid-Day Meals to nearby schools. Eligibility Criteria: 1. The applicant shall belong to SC/ST, SMF, and BPL Families. 1. The applicant must have the back ground of poultry farming, or in other cases, the participants must undergo practical training. 1. The applicant must operate the units on the scientific lines as per the technical guidance and services provided by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, Daman & Diu. 1. The applicant must operate the unit for at least for the minimum period of two years. 1. The applicant shall have to maintain the prescribed records and furnish the prescribed information to the Veterinary Officer, Daman & Diu, from time to time. 1. The applicant shall have to follow the Instructions issued by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, Daman & Diu. 1. The applicant shall have to execute a bond to the effect that the aforesaid terms and conditions are acceptable and he/it will abide by all of them, failing which he will be liable to be prosecuted as per the existing rules of the Administration. 1. The applicant has to compulsorily sale/supply the surplus eggs to the nearby school under the scheme of Mid-Day Meals.
Benefits: Financial Assistance In The Form Of Subsidy Financial assistance in the form of a subsidy shall be provided to the individual beneficiary on the following items: Construction of poultry shed. Purchase cost of reared pullets up to the age of 18-21 weeks old. Poultry equipments. Purchase cost of feed for the period of 4 months (till the beneficiary starts earning from the sale price of egg produce). Each beneficiary will be provided 50% subsidy to the total cost of the unit (i.e., total cost of purchase of Pullets, poultry feed, poultry equipments and construction of poultry shed, etc.), limited to ₹30,000/- per unit. The beneficiary will be entitled to get the benefit of the scheme for a period of two years or till he becomes self-sufficient. The financial assistance should be used only for the purpose for which it may be granted. Disbursement of Funds Subsidy will be paid directly to the individual or to the suppliers or to the body supplying goods or to an approved agency or institution. The Veterinary Officer, Daman & Diu, would disburse the assistance in the form of a subsidy after completion of the poultry unit in respect of the construction of a poultry shed, which should be of low-input technology. Purchase of Pullets, feed, or equipment directly to the individual supplier, body, or an approved agency or institution. The Extension Officer (Dairy) or Veterinary Officer (DP) will make a fortnightly payment to the beneficiary for the supply of eggs regularly. Subsidy shall be disbursed after completion of the poultry unit. The beneficiary will be entitled to get the benefit of the scheme for a period of two years or till he becomes self-sufficient.

To provide a regular supply of healthy eggs under the Scheme of Mid-Day Meals to nearby schools.
Financial Assistance In The Form Of Subsidy
Financial assistance in the form of a subsidy shall be provided to the individual beneficiary on the following items:
Construction of poultry shed.
Purchase cost of reared pullets up to the age of 18-21 weeks old.
Poultry equipments.
Purchase cost of feed for the period of 4 months (till the beneficiary starts earning from the sale price of egg produce).

Each beneficiary will be provided 50% subsidy to the total cost of the unit (i.e., total cost of purchase of Pullets, poultry feed, poultry equipments and construction of poultry shed, etc.), limited to ₹30,000/- per unit.
The beneficiary will be entitled to get the benefit of the scheme for a period of two years or till he becomes self-sufficient.
The financial assistance should be used only for the purpose for which it may be granted.
Disbursement of Funds
Subsidy will be paid directly to the individual or to the suppliers or to the body supplying goods or to an approved agency or institution.

The Veterinary Officer, Daman & Diu, would disburse the assistance in the form of a subsidy after completion of the poultry unit in respect of the construction of a poultry shed, which should be of low-input technology.
Purchase of Pullets, feed, or equipment directly to the individual supplier, body, or an approved agency or institution.
The Extension Officer (Dairy) or Veterinary Officer (DP) will make a fortnightly payment to the beneficiary for the supply of eggs regularly.
Subsidy shall be disbursed after completion of the poultry unit.
The beneficiary will be entitled to get the benefit of the scheme for a period of two years or till he becomes self-sufficient.
In case of breach of any of the terms and conditions, the entire amount of assistance shall be recoverable from the beneficiaries as per law (subject to Dadra & Nagar Haveli Jurisdiction).
Step 1:

The eligible SC/ST, SMF, and BPL family beneficiary shall participate in the scheme and must have the back ground of poultry farming or, in other cases, undergo practical training provided by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, if required.
Step 2:

The beneficiary shall establish the poultry unit, including the construction of a poultry shed (of low input technology), the purchase of reared pullets up to the age of 18–21 weeks old, poultry equipments and the purchase of feed for the period of 4 months (till the beneficiary starts earning from the sale price of egg produce).
Step 3:

The units under this scheme shall be operated on scientific lines as per technical guidance and services provided by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, Daman & Diu, and shall be operated at least for a minimum period of two years.
Step 4:

After completion of the small-scale poultry unit, a completion certificate shall be obtained from the Field Level Worker i.e., Veterinary Stockman or Extension Officer (Dairy), and the certificate shall be countersigned by the concerned Veterinary Officer (D.P) or Veterinary Officer (Animal Husbandry).
Step 5:

The Veterinary Officer, Daman & Diu shall disburse the assistance in the form of subsidy after completion of the poultry unit in respect of the construction of poultry shed and purchase of pullets, feed or equipment directly to the individual supplier or body or an approved agency or institution, or to the individual beneficiary as applicable.
Step 6:
The beneficiary shall compulsorily sale/supply the surplus eggs to the nearby school under the scheme of Mid-Day Meals.
Step 7:
Extension Officer (Dairy) or Veterinary Officer (DP) will do a fortnightly payment to the beneficiary for regular supply of eggs.

Scheme Name: Integrated Dairy Development Project (IDDP) Short Title: IDDPDAMAN Detailed Description: The “Integrated Dairy Development Project (For 2 Cows)” scheme has been launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, U.T. Administration of Daman & Diu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli. The scheme aims to promote dairy development through the introduction of Gir breed milch cows and the provision of necessary dairy inputs. Through this scheme, financial assistance and subsidies are provided to beneficiaries for the purchase of cows, cattle shed infrastructure, feed, mineral mixture, and insurance coverage. Eligibility Criteria: 1. The applicant must be a resident of the Union Territory of Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. 1. The applicant should purchase only the Indigenous Gir breed milch cows. 1. The applicant should utilise the grant only for the purpose for which it is sanctioned and within the stipulated period. 1. The applicant should maintain all required records and registers as per the General Financial Rules, 1963. 1. The applicant should submit utilisation certificates, audited accounts, and achievement reports as prescribed by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services. > **Preference / Reservation:** - A higher subsidy rate is applicable for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe applicants.
Benefits: Sr. No. Activity Cost (₹) UT Subsidy Admin (₹) Under DEDS – Subsidy Beneficiary Gets 1 Cost of 2 milch cows of the Indigenous “Gir” breed, including transportation cost (@ ₹60,000/- per animal) ₹1,20,000/- ₹30,000/- (@25% of purchase cost subject to a maximum of ₹30,000/-) Beneficiary will get back-ended subsidy from NABARD @ 25% for General and 33.33% for SC/ST, i.e. ₹30,000/- (@25% for General) or ₹39,996/- (@33.33% for SC/ST) 2 Cost towards cattle shed, water tank with automatic drinking system (already existing) ₹8,000/- ₹4,000/- (50% of construction cost) - 3 44 bags of cattle feed (each of 50 kg) (44 bags × 2) (@ ₹600/- per bag) ₹52,800/- ₹26,400/- (50% of purchase cost) - 4 44 kg of mineral mixture (each of 1 kg) (44 kg × 2) (@ ₹80/- per bag) ₹7,040/- ₹3,520/- (50% of purchase cost) - 5 Cost of insurance for 3 years (approx. @ ₹5,400/- per animal) ₹10,800/- ₹5,400 (50% for General) or ₹8,100 (75% for SC/ST) - Total ₹1,98,640/- ₹69,320/- (General) or ₹72,020/- (SC/ST) ₹99,320/- (General) or ₹1,12,016/- (SC/ST)
